definition: The Egyptian concept of truth, balance, and right order, personified as a goddess. Maat was what the gods loved and what the king was meant to maintain.
One of the components of a person, often translated as vital force or double. The ka was sustained by food offerings and could dwell in a statue of the deceased.
The mobile aspect of a person, often shown as a human-headed bird. The ba travelled between the tomb and the underworld.
The hidden underworld through which the sun god travelled each night. The dead also passed through the Duat, guided by funerary texts.
The company of nine deities of Heliopolis: Atum, Shu, Tefnut, Geb, Nut, Osiris, Isis, Set, and Nephthys. The word comes from the Greek for nine.
The primeval mound that rose from the waters of Nun, and the sacred stone at Heliopolis that represented it. Pyramids were thought to echo its shape.
The title of Egypt's king, understood as a living god and the upholder of Maat. The word originally meant great house, the royal palace.
A dung beetle associated with the sun god and with rebirth. Scarab amulets were placed on mummies and inscribed with protective spells.
A modern name for collections of Egyptian funerary spells meant to guide the dead safely into the afterlife. Copies were customized, so they vary widely.
The Egyptian word usually translated as god or divine power. It could describe a deity, the king, or a sacred force in a place or object.
